claim: For every fixed integer \(k\ge 1\), deciding whether a sentence \(\varphi\) of monadic first-order logic with equality and the infinity quantifiers is monotone in a designated unary predicate \(P\), over possibly empty domains and with exactly \(k\) unary predicates in the input signature, is \(\mathrm{PSPACE}\)-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions. \(\mathrm{PSPACE}\)-hardness already holds for \(k=1\) in the first-order sublanguage without infinity quantifiers.
integrity_notes: The proof is symbolic and does not rely on finite experiments or generated certificates.
No independent audit or independent validation is claimed.
scientific_limitations: The polynomial-space upper bound is for each fixed number \(k\) of unary predicates; no uniform polynomial exponent in that number is claimed.
The result does not cover binary predicates, function symbols, or other generalized quantifiers.

The first_public_date is the first public date of the foundational ME-infinity source used for the direction; the fixed-vocabulary complexity classification is proved in this finding, not attributed to that source.
title: Fixed-vocabulary monotonicity in monadic logic with the infinity quantifier is \(\mathrm{PSPACE}\)-complete
